intro: Physical therapists combine clinical judgment with teaching and patient care. The closest of the 25 careers below is Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary, with a 79% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $107,310, which is 4% more than the $102,760 physical therapists earn.
why_it_works: Every session you assess movement, explain exercises and keep patients motivated through slow progress. O*NET rates social perceptiveness and service orientation at 4 out of 5 for this job. That is why teaching, genetic counseling and therapy assistant roles come out close. Your pay is already high, so only 2 matches pay more. The new skills are mostly instructing groups, research and some programming.
tips: Teach a clinical course or supervise students first; it tests whether college teaching suits you.
Look at health informatics if you like data: Health Informatics Specialists earn $105,850 for their broader group.
Keep your license active while you explore, so you can return to practice if needed.

faq.q: What jobs can former physical therapists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are postsecondary health specialties teachers (79%), Genetic Counselors (75%) and nursing instructors (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Occupational Therapy Assistants are 71% matched but earn $72,300, which is 30% less than the $102,760 physical therapist median.

faq.q: Which careers for physical therapists pay more?
faq.a: Only 2 of the 25 matches pay more. Health specialties teachers earn $107,310 (4% more) and Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists earn $103,410 (1% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Clinical Research Coordinators earn $167,220 for their broader BLS group.

faq.q: Do physical therapists need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than physical therapists already have. A master's or doctoral level is common: in a close match, 91% of workers hold a master's degree, so your clinical degree already covers most options.

faq.q: What skills should physical therapists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, complex problem solving, programming and coordination. Judgment already rates 3.75 out of 5 for physical therapists in O*NET, so research, teaching and data skills are the main step for most of these moves.
